payload.description:
## Context

The owner requires repository-owned onboarding for persistent agent memory.
One person configures the repository and commits all required shared setup.
Other machines receive the instructions, skills and bootstrap through clone or pull.
Agents must establish tracker context before implementation. Missing memory must stop work.
Related feature: basicly-gtb19bg.43.

## Scope

Detect missing machine setup from committed repository guidance and executable startup paths.
Configure the existing tracker without repeating repository migration.
Cover standalone and harness entrypoints. Preserve unrelated settings and frozen history.
Stop with a named remedy when prerequisites, permissions or vault access prevent setup.
Do not claim arbitrary third-party agents are blocked without an actual enforcement path.

## Confirmation Plan

Use public installer and agent-start regressions with fresh homes and repository copies.
Exercise clone, pull introduction, successful bootstrap, repeated startup and unavailable context.
Run affected standalone, agent installation, hook and consumer checks.
Keep existing gates and original concurrency tests unchanged.

payload.description:
## Finding
Reported by the handily session on 2026-11-16 at 15:10 UTC and reproduced by the basicly session.
A fresh install of released 0.46.1 in an empty repository refuses its own first commit.
The pre-commit catalog lint prints:

    catalog lint: FAILED
      .basicly/core/skills/agent-mail/skill.yaml: model-invoked skill 'agent-mail' is declared by no agent, so the engine inlines it into no dispatch prompt and the guidance reaches no role; add it to an agent's claude.skills, or — if no role should carry it — to skill_pairing.UNPAIRED_EXEMPTIONS with the reason

## Reproduction
Scratch folder, scratch HOME, normal PATH that holds a global basicly 0.45.0 (uv tool install).

    git init -q -b main
    printf '[hooks.markdownlint]\nenabled = false\n' > basicly.toml
    uvx --python '>=3.14' --from https://github.com/niksavis/basicly/releases/download/v0.46.1/basicly-0.46.1-py3-none-any.whl basicly install
    git add -A
    git commit -m 'chore: install basicly'

Install exits 0 with 'repo converged'. The commit exits 1 with the output above.

## Control
Same repository and commit, PATH without the global basicly, uv and uvx still reachable.
The commit exits 0 and prints 'catalog lint: OK'. The hook then used the uvx 0.46.1 wheel.

## Cause
.basicly/core/hooks/catalog-lint.py _cli_command takes shutil.which('basicly') first.
It uses the install-state version (uvx from dist_source) only when no basicly is on PATH.
A global basicly 0.45.0 lints the 0.46.1 catalog.
The agent-mail skill and its UNPAIRED_EXEMPTIONS entry in src/basicly/skill_pairing.py first shipped in v0.46.0 (c5d9ebf5).
So the older engine does not know the exemption and refuses.
Main at fb6c2341 has the same fault: the hook body is unchanged since v0.46.1.
tracker-fold.py and session-start.py also take shutil.which('basicly') first and may share the skew.

## Impact
Every consumer with an older global basicly fails the first commit after an install or upgrade.
Onboarding of development, basicly, handily and terminal starts from a fresh install, so this blocks it.
Separate, not fixed here: install refuses at once without markdownlint and writes nothing; the documented opt-out was used.

[design note 2026-11-16, basicly session, no code] Burst margin: two protocol options

Measured baseline (Trace2 plus a span profiler on the unchanged test; deadline, clone count, latency and workers unchanged):
- The last publisher in line needs 13 push rounds. The injected floor is 13 x 1.5 s = 19.5 s.
- Per round it also waits 0.3-0.45 s for a fetch. That fetch already started before the rejection in 86 of 91 matched waits.
- Real push: 0.045 s alone, 0.24 s in the full suite on 4 CPUs, 0.49 s on 2 CPUs. On 2 CPUs the pre-push guard process is 0.39 s of it.
- One failing 2-CPU run started 5183 Git processes in 30 s. The 39 joiner threads made 297 of the 312 fetches.
- Slowest publisher: 27.1-29.65 s when passing, 29.9 s when failing. The smallest margin seen in a pass is 0.35 s.
- No single wasted step reached 5 s, so this is a protocol question and not a hotfix.

Option 1: joiners stop fetching; the publisher fetches once per round, during its push.
- Change: a joining session waits on the share lock holder's progress file instead of running its own helper refresh. The publisher starts one fetch beside each push, so the retry overlap stays.
- Expected gain: 0.5 to 3 s on 2 CPUs, about 0 to 1 s on 4 CPUs (assumed). Basis: about 60 % of runner calls and 95 % of fetches come from joiners. Real push time scales with load (0.24 s at 4 CPUs, 0.49 s at 2 CPUs). The gain assumes queue time falls with process count, which is not measured. It can lose up to 1.8 s if the publisher fetch overlaps less than the joiner fetches do now.
- Size: 6 to 10 hours (assumed), including the join-path tests.
- Risk: the takeover and joined-claim paths depend on joiner refresh (test_a_live_sharer_finishes_after_takeover..., test_a_joined_claim_reserves_time...).

Option 2: one ref per writer, so publishers stop competing for main.
- Change: each clone pushes its batch to its own ref, so a push is never rejected. A deterministic fold orders competing claims, for example by the first canonical event. The push guard accepts the writer ref instead of refusing other branches.
- Expected gain: about 15 to 18 s. Basis: 13 rounds become 1, so the injected cost per publisher falls from 19.5 s to 1.5 s, and the retry waits (4 to 5 s) go away.
- Size: 3 to 5 days (assumed). It is a vault protocol change: claim ordering semantics, guard rules, migration of existing vaults, and the old-kit compatibility that basicly-wecjejf tracks.
- Risk: this is a new protocol after release. It conflicts with the frozen 0.46 vault format and needs an owner decision on scope.

Proof that is not luck, for either option:
- Run the unchanged burst test 30 times in each of three conditions: alone on 4 CPUs, the full suite on 4 CPUs, and the vault files with -n 4 on 2 CPUs.
- Record the slowest publisher span of every run, not the pass count.
- Accept only when the minimum margin (30 s minus the slowest span) is at least 5 s in every condition, and the median moves by more than the run-to-run spread of the baseline.
- Measure the baseline distribution first under the same three conditions. Today's smallest passing margin is 0.35 s.

The design note with two options and the proof method is a comment on basicly-gtb19bg.43.42 (pushed at 50a8cdee).

1. Joiners stop fetching, and the publisher fetches once per round. Gain 0.5-3 s on 2 CPUs (assumed). Size 6-10 h.
